claim: Daily Habits is an abandoned free habit tracker: last updated 18 May 2021 (v1.5.1), 517 reviews across 61 storefronts, 299 US ratings at 4.40
this_app_does: developer Olha Ievenko / XWaveSoft, bundle com.xwavesoft.habits; sibling apps Be Focused and Focus Matrix; free download, ad-supported, one-time Pro
magnitude: 517 reviews, 61 storefronts, Nov 2016 → Aug 2026; 299 US ratings at 4.40; last update 18 May 2021

claim: Method: signal bands applied against two denominators only (all 517, and the US n=98 — the only storefront over the 50-review bar); one review = 0.19%, so every band boundary is soft
magnitude: 60 other storefronts hold 419 reviews (mean 4.23) — counted globally, no standalone claims; bands <0.1 ignore / 0.1–0.5 weak / 0.5–1 emerging / 1–3 meaningful / 3–5 very strong / >5 high-priority
conditions: a five-review swing moves a theme a full band

claim: A well-liked, genuinely differentiated free habit tracker was killed by data loss, crashes and five years of silence — and its headline rating went UP while it died
magnitude: executive summary; supporting numbers in R02-004..008
side_effects: a rising store rating can hide a dying product

claim: Development stopped in May 2021 — 5 years 4 months without an update — and reviewers had been noticing since 2019
magnitude: 9 explicit abandonment complaints (1.74%, mean 2.89), from 2019 (DE, NI) to 2026 (IT)
side_effects: users read silence as abandonment years before the store listing shows it

claim: Review volume fell 96% (100/yr in 2019 → 4 in 2026) while the mean rose from 4.19 to 4.31 — survivorship, not recovery; nothing shipped after May 2021
side_effects: do not read a rising average as improvement when volume collapses

claim: The US — the largest and richest market — is the worst-rated one (3.80 vs 4.15 global, 23.5% 1–2★ vs 15.1%); Japan worse still at 3.30; the highest-rating markets write the shortest reviews
magnitude: US mean 3.80, 23.5% 1–2★; global 4.15, 15.1%; JP 3.30 [limited evidence n=20]; BR 4.65, GB 4.45 with shortest reviews
side_effects: engaged Western users are the honest signal

claim: A quarter of the corpus carries almost no product information: 132 reviews (25.5%) under 40 characters averaging 4.52 — short reviews inflate the rating; Vietnam is 14 reviews, 13 of them 5★, mostly 'Good' / 'Ok'
magnitude: 132 (25.5%) under 40 chars, mean 4.52 vs corpus 4.15; VN 14 reviews, 13 5★, mean 4.93

claim: The launch window (Nov–Dec 2016) looks partly seeded: generic non-native 5★ reviews within days of release, two reviewers called it out, and a free-Pro giveaway ran at launch
this_app_does: possibly seeded launch reviews + free-Pro giveaway at launch
magnitude: Nov–Dec 2016 = 65 reviews at 4.32 / 66.2% 5★ vs 4.12 / 60.0% for the rest; inference from style and timing, not proof
side_effects: 'the obviously machine-translated 5-star reviews actually make a bad impression' (JP); 'the positive reviews are LIES' (RU) — seeded reviews are noticed and cost trust
conditions: discount the first two months rather than treating them as baseline

claim: The honest read is ~3.8–4.0 among engaged Western users, and the decline is entirely self-inflicted through reliability, not competition
Free download, ad-supported, with an unusually generous free tier — unlimited habits — which is the app's single strongest differentiator and is given away
this_app_does: unlimited habits free; ads in free tier
magnitude: unlimited-habits praise is the top theme (5.80%, Part 3)
conditions: report calls the free tier 'too good relative to a broken Pro' (§1.6 #3) — the problem is Pro, not the free tier

claim: Pro is a one-time in-app purchase — US $3.99 (2016), ~$4 CAD, €1 in a promo — repeatedly described as 'minuscule' / 'cheap'
magnitude: price points from 5 reviews; 19 buyers cite one-time fee (§1.3)

claim: One reviewer calls it a subscription; isolated and contradicted by the listing and by 18 other reviewers praising the one-time fee — treat as reviewer error

conditions: the Pro headline feature; 6 buyers name it as the reason they paid (§1.3)

claim: Support flipped: every positive support mention is from 2016–2018 ('kept the promise of responding in 48 hours', 'support persisted with me and it worked'); every negative one is later or unanswered ('I click on App Support, nothing happens')
side_effects: a 48-hour response promise, kept, earns rating upgrades; an App Support link that does nothing is noticed

claim: No AI-related expectation appears anywhere in the corpus — zero mentions across 517 reviews and 11 years
Local-first, durable storage with a restore path — data loss is 4.26% at mean 1.95 and is what turned paying customers into refund requests; no feature matters more
Never let the app freeze on check-off; tap latency must not grow with habit count — Japan's payers waited 5+ seconds
this_app_does: crashes; lag grows with habit count

claim: Get the date right in every surface and every timezone — widget, Watch and app must agree; this developer solved it once
If you ship an Apple Watch app, it must actually sync — 12 of 15 Watch mentions are failures at mean 2.33, and it was a stated purchase reason
Never write to the user's calendar without exact, reversible, correctly-sized events — one user needed Apple support to repair their phone
Keep the one-time purchase — 19 reviews at mean 4.84 name it as the reason to buy; the app's only durable competitive weapon against subscription rivals
Do not gate the habit cap — unlimited-free is the highest-rated theme in the corpus (mean 4.97) and earns the word-of-mouth a tiny marketing budget cannot buy
conditions: evidence: R02-037, R02-047; contrast report 1 (cap of 6+ held constant)

claim: Make the paid tier things that actually work — this app charged for sync, calendar and stats, shipped all three broken, and paying users ended a full star below free ones; ship the paid feature before you sell it
Fix the purchase flow — 1.55% of all reviews are people who tried to give money and couldn't
'X times per week' scheduling — the single most-requested model change and a churn cause on its own
Manual habit reordering — trivial to build, requested for eight straight years, mean 4.33
Customisable, louder reminder sounds — the cheapest 5★ upgrade available
Weekly / monthly / yearly review screens — the top 4★ blocker
Keep personal photos on habits — rare, loved, and no competitor in this corpus offers it
Onboarding — a skippable, replayable tour of swipe-to-complete and the break-a-habit toggle
Lead with 'unlimited habits, free, no subscription' — it is what every advocate in this corpus says unprompted
magnitude: the two era-D themes at 8.2% each

claim: If you have sibling apps, integrate them or say plainly that you don't — assumed integration drove purchases that ended in 1★
Do not ship and walk away — abandonment is visible to users within about a year and the app becomes an iOS-release liability for paying users with no recourse
magnitude: abandonware 1.74%; iOS 14 broke it for payers

claim: Do not spam rating prompts or cross-promote to paying customers
Do not seed launch reviews — two users spotted it in week one and said so publicly, and it permanently contaminates your own analytics baseline

Method: 517 records, zero duplicates, 100% reconciliation with by_country and manifest; all reviews read in full in 17 languages; regex candidates then hand-curated ID lists (false positives: 'add' vs ADHD, 'productive' vs the app); non-exclusive theme membership; one external source (Apple lookup API, 2026-09-09); n=517 is small (one review = 0.19%); only the US clears 50; eras have shrinking samples (164/161/107/85)
conditions: report 2 uses the older part structure (Parts 0–8 + Appendix, no Part 9)

claim: A support path that actually responds: early users praised a kept 48-hour response promise and upgraded ratings; later users found 'App Support' did nothing and paying users lost data with no reply
magnitude: 6 positive support IDs (2016–18) vs 3 unanswered later; 'no support reply' inside the 1★ payer list

claim: The Apple Watch app is simultaneously a stated purchase driver ('far superior to other habit trackers') and 80% broken (12 of 15 mentions negative, mean 2.33) — same feature, both directions, decided by reliability alone

This report says 'do not gate the habit cap' (unlimited free, mean 4.97); report 1 says 'set the cap generously (6+) and leave it alone' because unlimited is its #2 purchase reason — the two apps resolve the free-cap question differently
magnitude: here: unlimited-free 5.80% at 4.97; report 1: cap complaints ×7.5 on 2★ but 'unlimited' #2 purchase reason
conditions: what both agree on: never change the cap once set; see Research Reports/Feature Gating vs Quantity.md

claim: A free-Pro giveaway ran at launch (Nov 2016); it inflated early sentiment, and for at least three users the promo failed to apply — one paid the $3.99 anyway
magnitude: 3 giveaway IDs; 3 'promo failed to apply' IDs
side_effects: a promo that does not apply reliably produces 2–3★ from people who wanted the product

claim: Completion feedback is locked in the free tier — a user who otherwise liked the app left 3★ because free gives no feedback on completing a habit
conditions: core-loop feedback (the reward for checking off) gated behind Pro reads as a broken free tier
